sourceArticle.title: Why Creators Are Letting Claude Run Their Entire Video Workflow
sourceArticle.author: Julian Horsey

athenaOutput.directive: Initiate the architectural design and implementation of the Creative Liberation Engine's native, self-hosted AI Video Studio (IEVS), commencing with the Creative Liberation Engine Video Core (IEVC) for generative video capabilities and the Creative Liberation Engine Asset Library (IEAL) for integrated brand asset management.
athenaOutput.rationale: To fully embody Article I (Sovereignty) and Article IX (Ship Complete or Don't Ship), the Creative Liberation Engine must develop its own robust, end-to-end AI video production pipeline. This approach eliminates reliance on external platforms or models for core functionality, ensuring complete ownership and control. This initial phase will lay the foundational capabilities for automated, high-quality video content creation, directly addressing the advanced features highlighted in the provided article.

options.title: Build a dedicated, modular Creative Liberation Engine Video Studio (IEVS)
options.description: Design and implement a comprehensive, self-hosted AI video generation and branding system within the Creative Liberation Engine. This involves developing or integrating open-source foundational models for video synthesis, a robust asset management system for brand consistency, and an initial workflow orchestration layer. This will include the Creative Liberation Engine Video Core (IEVC) for generative capabilities, the Creative Liberation Engine Asset Library (IEAL) for brand assets, and the Creative Liberation Engine Workflow Orchestrator (IEWO) for process management.
options.tradeoffs: High initial development cost and complexity. Requires significant BOLT and AURORA resources for custom development and integration of advanced AI models.

options.title: Integrate and heavily customize an existing open-source AI video framework
options.description: Identify a mature, extensible open-source AI video generation framework (e.g., based on Stable Diffusion Video, or similar emerging technologies) and integrate it deeply into the Creative Liberation Engine. Customize it to meet our specific requirements for branding, content types, and workflow, ensuring it can be fully self-hosted and controlled.
options.tradeoffs: Potentially faster initial setup than building entirely from scratch, but still requires significant customization effort. Potential for upstream dependency issues or limitations imposed by the chosen framework's architecture.

options.title: Rely on external AI video APIs (e.g., direct Claude/Higgsfield integration)
options.description: Develop an integration layer to leverage third-party AI video generation services and platforms, acting as a wrapper to their APIs.
options.tradeoffs: Quickest to market, but fundamentally violates Article I (Sovereignty) and introduces critical external dependencies, security risks, and potential vendor lock-in. Offers no long-term strategic advantage or ownership.

veraOutput.verdict: The ATHENA DIRECTIVE and its RATIONALE are factually accurate and internally consistent. The directive clearly outlines the architectural design and implementation of the Creative Liberation Engine's native, self-hosted AI Video Studio (IEVS), including the Creative Liberation Engine Video Core (IEVC) and Creative Liberation Engine Asset Library (IEAL). The rationale logically supports this by referencing Article I (Sovereignty) and Article IX (Ship Complete or Don't Ship), emphasizing the need for complete ownership and control over the AI video production pipeline. This aligns with previously validated ATHENA decisions.
